input_origin.reuse: Exact existing 40000-example world and 43000-query panels; do not merge with the 25000-example variant

authorization: 2026-10-19 user explicitly authorized training the two parameter-free decode-rule gate arms (stability, readiness) from scratch, 1500000 steps each, on the existing data with the unchanged ordinary training; existing raw DiscoLoop and fixed-q-plus-u runs are reused as comparators.

gate_definition.handoff: X + u(H)(H-X) + q(H) at nonfinal rounds, q = unchanged DiscoLoop decoded feedback at strength one; final round reads raw H
gate_definition.stability: u_t(r) = sum_v p_r(t,v) p_{r-1}(t,v); p_r = softmax(E LN_f(H_r)) at token t; p_0 = one-hot input token
gate_definition.readiness: c_t(r) = 1 if token t attends to no earlier position with head-mean round-r attention >= tau, else s_t(r) * min over those sources of c_j(r-1); c(0)=1; u=c; attention recomputed in float32 from the shared block Q/K on the round input
gate_definition.gradient: gate signals computed under no_grad; no gate parameters; the backbone is unchanged
gate_definition.source: src/llm_memory_editability/rule_gate.py; matches the zero-training pre-checks results/loop-decode-stability-gate-test-20261019 and results/loop-readiness-gate-test-20261019

primary: After 1500000 steps, compare graph-B three-hop full-vocabulary answer accuracy at R8 from a post-training R1-16 replay (frozen diagnostic code, zero training) for stability-u and readiness-u versus reused fixed-q-plus-u (learned u) and raw DiscoLoop (no u). R8 is primary because R4 can include the one-round transient documented in the report. Also report R4 from the native grid, graph-A held-out 3/4-hop, graph-B 2/4-hop, atomic retention, all 11 panels, full learning curves and answer+EOS; do not select a best checkpoint or inference horizon.

reading.workable: A rule gate is a workable entity-agnostic replacement if graph-A held-out 2-4 hop at R8 stay within 2 percentage points of fixed-q-plus-u and graph-B two/three-hop at R8 are not below fixed-q-plus-u.
reading.readiness_needed: If stability-u loses graph-A deep hops while readiness-u keeps them, the progress signal is necessary when trained from scratch.
reading.neither: If both lose graph-A deep hops or graph-B composition, these entity-agnostic signals are insufficient under this recipe; this does not exclude other progress signals.

execution_policy.reason: Follow the previous gate ablation: CPU contracts and one discarded CUDA graph engineering update per arm precede train then grid. W&B learning-curve tracking online. The R1-16 replay after training is zero-training diagnosis with the frozen replay code.

limits: One previously observed development world and initialization; within-task architecture comparison, not evidence of natural-language generality.

Both new arms start from the same initial backbone as fixed-q-plus-u (no gate parameters). With near-uniform early decodes the stability value is about 1/vocab, so early training passes mostly decoded feedback; this is a property of the rule, not tuned.
The rule is detached: the model cannot directly optimize the gate signal, only adapt its decodes and attention through the forward effects.
Comparators were trained earlier on other hosts/runs; matching recipe and exposure does not imply bitwise runtime equivalence.
Rule computation adds forward-only matrix work (an extra vocabulary decode per boundary; readiness also Q/K/V and QK^T). Report wall time and FLOP estimates separately.
No learned controller, intermediate loss, curriculum, randomized depth, early exit, seed sweep or new-world training.
